alabama.rufada_status: Alabama has adopted RUFADAA as the Revised Uniform Fiduciary Access to Digital Assets Act, Act 2017-316 (HB 138), effective January 1, 2018, codified at Ala. Code §§ 19-1A-1 through 19-1A-18.
alabama.custodian_access: A fiduciary (personal representative, trustee, agent under a power of attorney, or conservator) can get the catalogue of electronic communications and other digital assets on a lighter showing, but the content of electronic communications only with the user's consent or a court order. The custodian may choose how to disclose: full account access, partial access, or a copy of the assets. It may demand a written request, a certified death certificate, proof of appointment such as letters testamentary, and the will, trust, or power of attorney showing consent, and it must comply within 60 days of a valid request.
alabama.user_direction: A user can direct disclosure through a custodian's online tool, or in a will, trust, power of attorney, or other record. The priority order is: online tool first, then will, trust, or power of attorney, then the custodian's terms of service.
alabama.terms_of_service: A direction made through an online tool or in a will, trust, or power of attorney overrides a contrary term in the custodian's terms of service. If the user left no direction at all, the terms of service govern, and the fiduciary then needs the user's consent in an estate document or a court order to reach the content of messages.
alabama.platform_tools: Google Inactive Account Manager lets a user name a trusted contact and set what happens after inactivity; Apple Legacy Contact lets a named person request access with a death certificate and an access key; Meta (Facebook and Instagram) lets a user name a legacy contact to manage a memorialized account or request removal. Each platform still requires its own form and proof of death, and a legacy-contact designation is treated as an online-tool direction.
alabama.what_to_do: 1. Make an inventory of accounts, devices, and crypto wallets. 2. Check each platform for an online-tool or legacy-contact designation. 3. Gather the will, trust, or power of attorney and the letters from the probate court. 4. Send each custodian a written request with a certified death certificate and proof of appointment. 5. If the custodian refuses or the content of messages is needed without consent, ask the probate court for an order.
alabama.agency_name: Alabama Attorney General, Consumer Interest Division
alabama.state_note: Alabama's act sits in Title 19 on fiduciaries rather than as a standalone technology law, and its custodian-disclosure section gives the custodian sole discretion to choose full access, partial access, or a copy of the assets.
sources: Ala. Code §§ 19-1A-1 through 19-1A-18 (Justia, 2025 Code of Alabama)
Alabama HB 138, Act 2017-316
Alabama Attorney General Divisions page

delaware.rufada_status: Delaware has NOT adopted RUFADAA. It has its own earlier law, the Fiduciary Access to Digital Assets and Digital Accounts Act, HB 345, Chapter 416 (2014), signed August 12, 2014 and amended in 2025 (SB 143), codified at 12 Del. C. §§ 5001 through 5007.
delaware.custodian_access: A fiduciary, including a personal representative, guardian, agent under a durable power of attorney, or trustee, may exercise control over any and all rights in the account holder's digital assets and digital accounts, to the extent permitted by state or federal law or an end-user license agreement. The custodian must comply with a valid written request within 30 days. Delaware does not use RUFADAA's catalogue-versus-content split, so access turns on the governing instrument, the fiduciary's authority, and applicable privacy law rather than on a separate consent rule for message content.
delaware.user_direction: Delaware has no RUFADAA-style online-tool priority rule: the words online tool and designated recipient do not appear in Chapter 50. A user directs access mainly through a governing instrument such as a will, trust, or power of attorney that grants the fiduciary authority over digital assets, or through a court order. Platform tools such as Google Inactive Account Manager, Apple Legacy Contact, and Meta legacy contact still work as the platform's own settings, but Delaware law does not rank them above a will or trust the way RUFADAA does.
delaware.terms_of_service: A fiduciary's control is expressly subject to applicable state or federal law and to any end-user license agreement, so a custodian's terms can limit access in Delaware in a way RUFADAA's priority rule would not allow. If the user left no direction at all, the fiduciary's authority comes from the will, trust, or power of attorney and the court, and a custodian may still refuse disclosure that federal privacy law or its license terms forbid.
delaware.platform_tools: Google Inactive Account Manager lets a user name a trusted contact and set what happens after inactivity; Apple Legacy Contact lets a named person request access with a death certificate and an access key; Meta (Facebook and Instagram) lets a user name a legacy contact to manage a memorialized account or request removal. Each platform still requires its own form and proof of death. Because Delaware has no online-tool statute, these tools operate under the platform's own policy rather than under a state priority rule.
delaware.what_to_do: 1. Make an inventory of accounts, devices, and crypto wallets, including usernames and passwords, which Delaware's definition of digital asset expressly includes. 2. Check each platform for a legacy-contact or inactive-account designation. 3. Gather the will, trust, or durable power of attorney that grants digital-asset authority and the appointment from the Register of Wills. 4. Send each custodian a written request with a certified death certificate and proof of appointment. 5. If the custodian refuses, ask the Court of Chancery or the appropriate court for an order.
delaware.agency_name: Delaware Department of Justice, Fraud and Consumer Protection Division, Consumer Protection Unit
delaware.state_note: Delaware was the first state in the nation to pass a digital-assets access law in 2014, a year before the Uniform Law Commission finished RUFADAA, and it kept its own broader law instead of adopting RUFADAA. Its definition of digital asset expressly includes usernames and passwords.
sources: 12 Del. C. §§ 5001 through 5007 (Delaware Code)
Delaware HB 345, 79 Del. Laws, Chapter 416, signed August 12, 2014 (Delaware General Assembly)
Delaware Department of Justice homepage
